short: Emperor of the French, whose wars and legal code reshaped Europe.
full:
Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor on 18 May 1804, having risen through the revolutionary armies to seize power five years earlier. As a commander he was exceptional — Austerlitz in 1805 is still studied as a model battle — and by 1812 he dominated continental Europe directly or through client states.

The invasion of Russia that year destroyed his Grande Armée, and defeat followed at Leipzig and finally Waterloo in June 1815. His durable legacy is administrative rather than military: the Napoleonic Code swept away feudal law and remains the foundation of civil law systems across Europe, Latin America and beyond. He died in exile on Saint Helena in 1821.
